interactionPlan.concept: How the mathematical parameters of a sinusoidal wave (amplitude, period, and phase) correspond to its physical dimensions and shape.
learningObjectives: The student will understand that amplitude is measured from the central equilibrium axis to the peak, rather than peak-to-trough.
The student will be able to explain how changing the period of a wave horizontally stretches or compresses its cycles.
The student will recognize that phase shifts the entire wave horizontally without altering its amplitude or period.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: Amplitude and period are independent horizontal and vertical scaling factors that fully dictate a wave's periodic geometry relative to the equilibrium line.

interactions.label: Amplitude (A)
interactions.effect: Scales the wave vertically. The vertical double-headed 'Amplitude' indicator arrow dynamically stretches from y=0 to the wave's peak.
interactions.teaches: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position (not the total peak-to-trough height).

interactions.label: Period (T)
interactions.effect: Compresses or stretches the wave horizontally. The horizontal double-headed 'Period' indicator arrow dynamically resizes to span exactly one full cycle between consecutive peaks.
interactions.teaches: Period represents the horizontal distance required for the wave to complete one full cycle of oscillation.

interactions.label: Phase (Shift)
interactions.effect: Shifts the entire wave and its peak-to-peak 'Period' indicator horizontally along the t-axis.
interactions.teaches: Phase determines the horizontal offset of the wave starting point, shifting the wave in time without changing its shape.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: A clean 2D line plot showing a continuous sine wave with axes labeled 's(t)' (vertical) and 't' (horizontal). Dynamic SVG annotations are critical: a vertical double-headed arrow spanning from y=0 to y=A labeled 'Amplitude', and a horizontal double-headed arrow spanning from the first positive peak to the second positive peak labeled 'Period'. These arrows must dynamically track the peaks as they move based on the slider values.
